research_rationale: Executive Order 11203 (30 FR 3417, signed 1965-03-12) lets a Treasury Department employee serving under a Schedule B appointment in a position concerned with the protective function (protection of the life and safety of the President, his immediate family and others for whom similar protective services are provided by law) have the appointment converted to a career appointment on the conditions in sections 1 to 5. I read the complete held text (the text layer of the govinfo Federal Register pages, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11203.txt; identity confirmed by the order number, title, date and FR Doc. line) and confirmed the 13-clause inventory. No clause has an end in the order's own terms: the alternative 90-day period in section 1(2) that runs from the date of the order was a transition for employees already qualified in 1965, while the alternative that runs from the date the employee meets the service requirement continues, and section 4 only sets the separation date for an employee who is not recommended or fails to qualify. The only held later instrument that names this order is Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28), whose section 2-101 lists Executive Order 11203 under subsection (b) and amends each listed order by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, effective 1979-01-01 under section 2-404. I record that substitution as an amendment on the three clauses that named the Commission (sections 1(3), 1(4) and 5); it is not an end. Current predicate: the U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order, as amended by Executive Order 12107, in a note to 5 U.S.C. 3301 with no ending statement, and 5 U.S.C. 3301 and 7301 (the successors of the statutes the order cites, as the note brackets them) are held in force at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt and usc-t5-s7301.txt. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog found no revocation, supersession or ending statement; the eCFR text of 5 CFR 9701.604 (Department of Homeland Security personnel system) and the Office of Personnel Management's 2024 consolidated listing of Schedule B exceptions (89 FR 61149, FR Doc. 2024-16723) both still refer to conversion under the order, which are recitals of continued use and not changes to it. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that search; the eCFR search is stated as of 2026-10-14. The U.S. Code note and the extracted Code and eCFR texts named above are leads: their original release-point bytes are not held, so the current-law basis cited in this claim is the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches.

Its own text has no savings or transition clause, and none of the held later texts that name it (Executive Order 12107) contains a savings clause that reaches it. Conversions already made are completed appointments, not continuing commands of the order.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12235 (45 FR 58803, signed 1980-09-03) delegates to the Secretary of Energy the President's functions under sections 301 to 304(c) of the Natural Gas Policy Act of 1978 (15 U.S.C. 3361-3364(c)) and section 607 of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (15 U.S.C. 717z), keeping to the President the authority to declare, extend and terminate a natural gas supply emergency, and adds consultation, redelegation and cooperation commands. I read the complete held text (the text layer of the govinfo Federal Register page, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12235.txt; identity confirmed by the order number, title, date, FR Doc. 80-27464 line and the 45 FR 58803 page heading). The held text layer joins the tail of section 1-102 with sections 1-103 and 1-104 in the scope the inventory calls sec1-102-a; I decide that scope as one unit and state each of its parts in its reason. No clause has an own-terms end. The order's own authority is section 304(d) of the Natural Gas Policy Act, and the current text of 15 U.S.C. 3364(d) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t15-s3364.txt, release point 119-121) still authorizes the President to delegate authority under sections 3361, 3362, 3363 and 3364 and to authorize redelegation. The same file prints Executive Order 12235 in its notes with no ending statement. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel prints the order in a note to 15 U.S.C. 3364 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09), and Table IV lists it there. The text of 15 U.S.C. 3361-3363 and 717z is not held; the claim does not rely on it beyond the cross-references in 15 U.S.C. 3364 (which still names sections 3361, 3362 and 3363) and on the point that the same release point marks repealed Code provisions with the word former (for example the note to 42 U.S.C. 5195 prints former 50 U.S.C. App. 2286(a)(4)) and does not do so for 15 U.S.C. 3361-3364 or 717z in this order's note; this is an inference from the editorial convention, not a finding that those sections are in force. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog and a search of the held texts for the order number found no amendment, revocation or supersession: the only other held text naming the order is the 1989 OFR codification, which prints it unamended. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that search. The U.S. Code note and the extracted Code text named above are leads: their original release-point bytes are not held, so the current-law basis cited in this claim is the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches.
